topic: Fleming's moldy dish led to penicillin (1928)
claim: In 1928 Fleming noticed a mold clearing bacteria from a dish; Oxford's team turned it into the first antibiotic drug.

beats.caption: One moldy dish
beats.vo: This moldy dish changed medicine forever.

beats.caption: Sept. 3, 1928
beats.vo: September third, 1928. Alexander Fleming returns from holiday to a stack of staph dishes.

beats.caption: The bacteria are gone
beats.vo: One dish has mold. And around it, the bacteria are gone.

beats.caption: Mold juice
beats.vo: He grows the mold alone. Its juice kills strep, meningococcus, even diphtheria.

beats.caption: Oxford, 1941
beats.vo: But it's unstable. Oxford's Florey and Chain turn it into medicine by 1941.

beats.caption: Nobel Prize, 1945
beats.vo: In 1945, Fleming, Florey and Chain share the Nobel Prize. One moldy dish began the antibiotic age.

sources.text: ACS International Historic Chemical Landmark: Discovery and Development of Penicillin, https://www.acs.org/education/whatischemistry/landmarks/flemingpenicillin.html
